title: Five kilometres for Lola
summary: Andrés hates running, but he agrees to do a charity race for his neighbour's little girl.
paragraphs: Andrés was not a runner. He didn't like sport, he didn't like getting up early, and he especially didn't like being out of breath. So when his neighbour asked him to join a five-kilometre {{charity}} race, he laughed. Then she told him why.

Her daughter, Lola, was six and had a rare illness. A hospital in the city was {{raising}} money to buy a new machine, and the race was part of it. Every runner needed friends and family to give money for each kilometre. Andrés stopped laughing. "When is it?" he asked. "In eight weeks," she said.

The first week was terrible. He ran for two minutes and walked for three, and after twenty minutes his legs hurt and his face was red. A woman with a pram passed him. But he kept going. He downloaded an app for {{beginners}} that told him when to run and when to walk. Every week the running parts got a little longer.

His friends started to notice. His sister gave twenty euros. People at work gave money and asked him every Monday how far he had run. His grandmother, who was eighty-two, sent him a message every morning: "Did you run today?" He didn't want to disappoint her, so he ran, even in the rain.

On the day of the race, Lola was at the finish line with a sign that said "GO ANDRÉS". He didn't run fast. Hundreds of people {{overtook}} him, including a man dressed as a banana. But he ran the whole five kilometres without stopping, and he raised six hundred euros. Lola gave him a {{medal}} made of paper. He still has it on his fridge, and he still runs, three times a week.

charity.meaning: an organisation that collects money to help people who need it

raising.meaning: collecting money for a good reason

beginners.meaning: people who are starting to learn something

overtook.meaning: went past someone who was going in the same direction

medal.meaning: a flat round piece of metal given as a prize

questions.question: Why did Andrés agree to run?
options: The race was raising money for a hospital machine that could help Lola.
He wanted to win a prize.
questions.explanation: The hospital was raising money to buy a machine, and the race was part of it.

questions.question: How did the app help him?
options: It told him when to run and when to walk.
It showed him the fastest route.
It sent messages to his grandmother.
It counted the money he raised.
questions.explanation: The app for beginners told him when to run and when to walk.

questions.question: Why did he run even in the rain?
options: He didn't want to disappoint his grandmother.
questions.explanation: His grandmother sent a message every morning, and he didn't want to disappoint her.

questions.question: What happened in the race?
options: He ran the whole race without stopping, but not fast.
He ran with a man dressed as a banana.
questions.explanation: Hundreds of people overtook him, but he ran the whole five kilometres without stopping.
